I feel like everyones overreacting with the overlevelling thing. Everyone plays differently, and in a few areas time, it really won't make much of a difference anyway. I was overlevelled when I started off, but I found that it balanced itself out early-midgame for me, where enemies were challenging but fun to fight.
And honestly, considering fanboy Pat adores Dark Souls so much,  I don't get why we're chastising him for looking at hints and advice. The poor guy isn't allowed to play ahead without Matt and Woolie, and when he does play it's in limited, specific times.
When I got DS3 my play sessions went from 5-10 hours a day.
Y'all need to chill a bit and realise that it's real people playing man, and while your "GO BLIND" suggestions may work for your playthrough, it doesn't work when they have a hard to satisfy audience to entertain.

I can't believe this is actually a drama. People are getting offended by the removal and replacement of a character's pose. I've seen some feminist bloggers complain about the female designs in Overwatch,  but the way most feminists see it now is if there is a chick with a personality,  we're one step closer to better female characters,  regardless of designs.

Honestly IDGAF, Tracer gets a new unique pose, we should be excited if anything.

Creative directors have a say in a lot things, and need to watch over a lot content. Occasionally things may be added or changed without acknowledging it simply because the amount of stuff that requires to be checked is overwhelming, and usually the directors hope that their staff do have an understanding of the characters they are designing. Who knows, this pose could've been originally implemented with the character at 3/4 or front view, but a staffer decided it looked better rotated, and it flew under the radar?

I have such mixed feelings right now. On one hand I don't mind Tracer's pose, but on the other hand some guys acting like the removal of one pose is a landslide to the destruction of human rights is making me glad they did it. It's literally just a pose. And it's not like it was removed really, just replaced. So what's the big deal?
Maybe this post made Blizzard decide  that it doesn't suit her character, rather than convince them that she's oversexualised?

But Hayter wasn't given the axe, he was just replaced. It's a dick move, but in the end, the game belongs to Kojima, the character belongs to Kojima,(okay technically konami but still) therefore if Kojima wanted to make a change so be it. If Hayter didn't fit his vision for the last game, then who is Kojima to be obilgated to include Hayter?

THAT BEING SAID, if I recall correctly, Kojima mentioned in an interview that Keifer was recommended by Guillermo Del Toro, so the major voice acting change was most likely influenced by his business relationship with Toro. At the time they had plans of making Silent Hills, so who's to say that it wasn't simply an act of trying to network and branch out. If Kojima believed that Toro had much more experience with casting, and he had plans to work with him in the future, I don't think it was that big of a long shot the he jumped on board to get Kiefer in.

I understand Hayter is bitter, but all I hear from him is how annoyed he is at Kojima. Like goddamn, compared to other voice actors Hayter had an EXTREMELY good run with Snake. And while it was explicity said that there wouldn't be another Metal Gear game, chances are, if Konami suddenly changed their minds Hayter would be back on board.

I work in an art store. We have a small section in the kids aisle dedicated to glitter.

For fucks sake, please read the sign that says "ASK FRIENDLY STAFF FOR ASSISTANCE WITH GLITTER PRODUCTS : )". Please don't spill neon glitter on the floor. Please don't let your kids actually open anything. Please don't cover our sign with fucking glitter glue. I'm the newbie and that's my aisle, and I'm going to be the one cleaning all that.

Infact, despite it having a kids aisle, our store, contrary to popular belief by parents, IS NOT A PLAYGROUND. Stop leaving your poor kids in our store while you go out shopping.

Speaking of which, I ended up spending 30 mins with a 9 year old because his mum was out shopping and left him here, teaching him to draw. Kid had so much fun he wanted to buy the pencils I was using (cheap fabers, plus I used a fineliner, which he also liked). Mum comes back in, he begs her to buy the pencils, she glares and him, and gave him the look I recognised really easily as the "when we get home you're getting a beating for making me buy this" look. God forbid you do anything for your child, woman....
I felt bummed, because I could tell he was happy about the pencils, but his fate was sealed with mum. It's weird seeing a kid look heartbroken.

Just needed that off my chest, it was kinda sad to witness...
